recipes.title: Risotto alla Milanese

ingredients.text: 1.5 l hot chicken or beef stock
ingredients.name: hot chicken or beef stock

steps: Crush the saffron and dissolve it in a ladle of the hot stock. Keep the rest of the stock simmering.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are glossy.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and letting each addition be absorbed before the next. After about 15 minutes stir in the saffron stock.
Cook until the rice is tender with a slight bite, about 18 minutes in total. The risotto should be creamy, not dry.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter and the parmesan. Rest 2 minutes and serve at once.

source.name: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene, no. 78
source.author: Pellegrino Artusi
source.license: Public domain (Project Gutenberg). Modern rewrite by this app.

recipes.notes: Artusi uses 500 g rice, 80 g butter, half an onion and saffron for five people, and says stock makes it richer. Parmesan is served with it.

recipes.title: Spinach Frittata
steps: Boil the spinach for 1 minute, plunge it into cold water, squeeze out all the water and chop roughly.
Melt half the butter in a 24 cm non-stick pan. Add the spinach, season and stir for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and the parmesan and pour them over the spinach.
Cook over medium-low heat for about 4 minutes until the underside is golden.
Slide the frittata onto a plate, melt the rest of the butter in the pan and turn the frittata back in. Cook 3 more minutes and serve warm or cold.

source.name: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene, no. 148
source.author: Pellegrino Artusi
source.license: Public domain (Project Gutenberg). Modern rewrite by this app.

recipes.notes: Artusi's proportions: 200 g spinach, 40 g butter and four eggs; a pinch of parmesan is optional.

recipes.title: Leek and Potato Soup
recipes.title_local: Soupe aux poireaux et pommes de terre

ingredients.text: 300 g leeks, white part only, finely sliced
ingredients.name: leeks

ingredients.text: 400 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
ingredients.name: potatoes

ingredients.text: 30 g baguette, thinly sliced and toasted
ingredients.name: baguette

steps: Melt 25 g butter in a large pot, add the leeks and stew gently for 15 minutes, covered, without colouring.
Add the potato slices and the stock, season lightly with salt and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Heat the milk to boiling in a separate pan and stir it into the soup.
Off the heat, stir in the cold butter so the soup turns silky. Taste for salt.
Serve in warm bowls with the toasted baguette slices floating on top.

source.name: A Guide to Modern Cookery, no. 751 (Soupe aux poireaux et pommes de terre)
source.author: Auguste Escoffier
source.license: Public domain (Project Gutenberg). Modern rewrite by this app.

recipes.notes: Converted from Escoffier's pints and ounces (1 pint = 570 ml). Use vegetable stock to make it vegetarian.

recipes.title: Fluffy Omelette (Mousseline)
steps: Beat the yolks with the salt and the cream.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the yolks.
Heat the butter in a 22 cm non-stick pan until foaming and pour in the mixture.
Cook over medium-high heat, drawing the set edges toward the centre, for about 2 minutes until just set but still soft on top.
Roll the omelette out of the pan onto a warm plate and serve immediately.

source.name: A Guide to Modern Cookery, no. 510 (Omelet Mousseline)
source.author: Auguste Escoffier
source.license: Public domain (Project Gutenberg). Modern rewrite by this app.

recipes.notes: Escoffier uses three eggs, one tablespoon of thick cream and 1 oz (30 g) butter.

recipes.title: Split Pea Soup with Smoked Pork

ingredients.text: 400 g smoked pork ribs or hock
ingredients.name: smoked pork ribs or hock

steps: Rinse the peas. Put them in a pot with the water and the smoked pork and bring to the boil.
Add the salt, cover and simmer for about 75 minutes, until the peas are soft and falling apart.
Lift out the meat. Purée the soup through a sieve or with a hand blender.
Cut the meat off the bones into small pieces, return it to the soup and heat through, stirring so it does not catch.
Fry the bread cubes in the butter until golden.
Stir the marjoram into the soup, taste for salt and serve with the croutons.

source.name: 365 obiadow za 5 zlotych, no. 18 (Zupa grochowa)
source.author: Lucyna Cwierczakiewiczowa

recipes.notes: The original pea-to-water ratio is 1:3 by volume and also gives a meatless version (use more peas, no pork).

recipes.title: Potato Cutlets
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft, drain and let them steam dry for 5 minutes.
Mash or rice the potatoes smooth, then mix in the cream, the 2 eggs, the 30 g butter and the salt.
Shape the mixture into 8 oval cutlets. Dip each in the beaten egg, then in the breadcrumbs.
Fry in the butter over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve with mushroom sauce or, as the author recommends, a sharp pickled-cucumber sauce.
